title.quote: Consistent Adversarially Robust Linear Classification: Non-Parametric Setting

analysis.description: This paper addresses the problem of adversarial robustness in binary linear classification without parametric assumptions, introducing a consistent estimator using Gaussian smoothing techniques. The research provides theoretical guarantees on the adversarial risk and shows that the estimator achieves minimax optimal rates.

type.justification: The paper is focused on the theoretical aspects of adversarially robust classification, exploring statistical methods and providing theoretical guarantees on consistency and optimal rates.
type.quote: Our work studies the non-parametric setting, where very little is known. With only mild regularity conditions on the conditional distribution of the features, we examine adversarial attacks with respect to arbitrary norms and introduce a straightforward yet effective estimator with provable consistency w.r.t adversarial risk.

name.justification: The paper discusses computing a Bayes-optimal robust linear classifier for binary classification problems under non-parametric assumptions.
name.quote: We now establish a deviation bound which proves that, for an appropriate sample-size dependent sequence of bandwidths h_n → 0, our proposed estimator f_b n,ε,h n ∈ F_lin defined in (13) is Bayes-consistent over the linear function class F_lin in the sense that its adversarial risk converges with large n to that of the optimal robust linear classifier.
